content: Fexofenadine is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis, commonly known as hay fever. These symptoms include a runny nose, sneezing, red or itchy eyes, watery eyes, and itching of the nose, throat, or roof of the mouth. It is suitable for adults and children aged 2 years and older. Additionally, fexofenadine is used to treat urticaria, also known as hives, which are red, itchy, raised areas on the skin. It helps relieve itching and rash in adults and children aged 6 months and older. Fexofenadine belongs to a class of drugs called antihistamines. It works by blocking the effects of histamine, a substance in the body that triggers allergy symptoms. Fexofenadine is available in tablet form and as a liquid suspension for oral use. It is typically taken with water once or twice daily. It is important to avoid taking fexofenadine with fruit juices such as orange, grapefruit, or apple juice, as these can reduce its effectiveness. The medication should be taken at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take fexofenadine exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. While fexofenadine helps control the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis and urticaria, it does not cure these conditions. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well and are not experiencing symptoms, as skipping doses may worsen your condition. If you are using the liquid suspension, shake it well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking fexofenadine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fexofenadine, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in the tablets or suspension. Your pharmacist can provide a list of the ingredients. Additionally, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as erythromycin (E-Mycin, Erythrocin) and ketoconazole (Nizoral), may require dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects when taken with fexofenadine. If you are taking an antacid containing aluminum or magnesium (e.g., Maalox, Mylanta), take it a few hours before or after fexofenadine. Inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking fexofenadine, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose of fexofenadine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fexofenadine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, vomiting, pain in the arms, legs, or back, menstrual pain, and cough. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects may occur. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, hoarseness, or difficulty swallowing or breathing. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, consult your doctor. Store fexofenadine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, drowsiness, and dry mouth. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
